title: Checkout discrete-event queue model
purpose: Represent individual requests through capacity-bounded servers, a bounded queue, deadlines, retries and backpressure so that latency, rejection and timeout behavior can be compared under a fixed workload.

includes: Bounded retries with backoff and jitter

abstraction.boundary: A request enters at its first arrival, occupies queue or server capacity until completion, timeout or rejection, and leaves after a terminal outcome.
abstraction.resolution: Event-level. Events are ordered by time, then priority, then insertion sequence.

state_variables.name: queue_length
state_variables.description: Requests waiting for a free server.

state_variables.name: completed
state_variables.description: Requests that reached a successful terminal outcome.

state_variables.name: failed
state_variables.description: Requests that exhausted their attempts or timed out terminally.

parameters.name: service_cv
parameters.note: Coefficient of variation for lognormal service time; not measured.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.note: Per-attempt deadline; not a measured client timeout.

parameters.name: bulkhead
parameters.note: Maximum total requests in queue and service.

equations: retry(t) = timeout_time + backoff(attempt) with optional jitter
reject(t) when queue_length >= queue_capacity or in_system >= bulkhead

invariants.name: request-conservation
invariants.statement: Every offered request is completed, rejected, failed, or still in the system at the horizon.

invariants.name: capacity-bound
invariants.statement: In-service requests never exceed the configured server count and waiting requests never exceed the queue capacity.

invariants.name: deadline-monotonic
invariants.statement: A timeout cannot complete a request after a successful completion at the same or an earlier timestamp.

cases.description: Same seed and inputs reproduce identical metrics and result hash.
Queue capacity zero rejects every request that cannot start service immediately.
Zero arrival rate produces no requests and no fabricated completions.
Request conservation holds across timeout, retry and rejection paths.

verification.notes: Verification covers the implemented event rules and boundary cases, not agreement with a production queue.

evidence.note: Candidate capacity, not a measured pool.

calibration.notes: All inputs are synthetic. No production trace, queue measurement or service-time sample was used.

validity_limits: Valid only for the synthetic arrivals, service distribution, timeout and capacity recorded in a scenario.
The model does not represent dependency calls, network retries or data consistency.
Results do not establish production latency, capacity or cost.
assumptions: Service times are independent across requests.
Retries re-enter the same queue and do not create a second request identity.
A timeout frees the server and may trigger a bounded retry.
unknowns: The real service-time tail and its correlation with load.
The real timeout distribution and client retry behavior.
The cost of a failed request versus a delayed successful request.
